summary: charge_confusion_rate.py control mode with --cl other than 68.27% wrote the Clopper-Pearson interval at --cl under interval_68 and its half-width as sign_rates rate_error, so a reader took, for example, a 95% half-width for a one-sigma error.

observables: control-mode sign_rates rate_error (passed on with sign_rates)
impact.bias: rate_error was the half-width at --cl instead of at 68.27%: at --cl 0.95 about 1.8 times too large (7 wrong-sign of 300: 0.0190 instead of 0.0105; 9.59e-4 instead of 5.12e-4 in the audit's bin), at --cl 0.5 too small; interval_68 held the --cl interval; status ok, no warning. The rate itself was right, and species_response.py from-rates does not read rate_error
impact.trigger: charge_confusion_rate.py control with --cl other than the default 0.6826894921370859; the bins carry interval_cl, which shows the --cl used

outputs.how_to_recognize: JSON on stdout of charge_confusion_rate.py control: bins[] with interval_68 and interval_cl different from 0.6826894921370859, and no 'interval' key; sign_rates rates[].rate_error; no artifact records the run

remedy: for runs with --cl other than the default, rerun on a version with the fix (or recompute the 68.27% Clopper-Pearson interval from each bin's n and k) and replace rate_error and interval_68 taken from them; rates are unchanged
